excerpts.text: In October 2015 Georgia participated in the first game of the [2018 Winter Olympic qualification tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ice_hockey_at_the_2018_Winter_Olympics_–_Men's_qualification "Ice hockey at the 2018 Winter Olympics – Men's qualification"), against [Bulgaria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bulgaria_men's_national_ice_hockey_team "Bulgaria men's national ice hockey team"), losing the match 9–1.[[14]](#cite_note-14) Funding from the Georgian government came for the first time in 2015; prior to that the players and management had to pay all expenses.[[9]](#cite_note-Qarsthusli-9) In the [2016 Division III tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_IIHF_World_Championship_Division_III "2016 IIHF World Championship Division III"), they finished second after winning four games out of five, only losing to [Turkey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turkey_men's_national_ice_hockey_team "Turkey men's national ice hockey team") 5–4, and having the tournament's leading scorer, Boris Kochkin (who had 10 goals and 9 assists).[[15]](#cite_note-15) However, all their matches were later nullified and the results recorded as 5–0 forfeits due to Georgia's use of ineligible players.[[16]](#cite_note-2016_ineligible-16) At the [2017 Division III tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_IIHF_World_Championship_Division_III "2017 IIHF World Championship Division III") they placed third, winning three of their five games.[[17]](#cite_note-17) Five Georgians placed in the top ten scorers, including Artem Kozyulin in first with 25 points (13 goals and 12 assists), while Artem Kurbatov was named the tournament's best defeceman.[[18]](#cite_note-18)[[19]](#cite_note-19) In the [2018 Division III tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_IIHF_World_Championship_Division_III "2018 IIHF World Championship Division III"), they finished first after winning four games out of five, losing one game to South Africa 4–2. Five of the top ten scorers in the tournament were from the Georgian team, including Aleksandr Zhuzhunashvili, who led the tournament in goals (10), assists (9), and points (19), and was named the best forward.[[20]](#cite_note-20)[[21]](#cite_note-21) For the first time, Georgia earned promotion to [Division IIB for 2019](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_IIHF_World_Championship_Division_II "2019 IIHF World Championship Division II"). The result was attributed to a policy of [naturalization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naturalization "Naturalization"): three of the top five scorers had Russian or Ukrainian surnames, while all five learned hockey outside of Georgia.[[22]](#cite_note-22) The result had Georgia place 40th in the [IIHF World Ranking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IIHF_World_Ranking "IIHF World Ranking"), their highest spot to date.[[23]](#cite_note-23)

excerpts.text:
[Georgia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgia_(country) "Georgia (country)") competed at the [2026 Winter Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Winter_Olympics "2026 Winter Olympics") in [Milan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milan "Milan") and [Cortina d'Ampezzo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cortina_d'Ampezzo "Cortina d'Ampezzo"), Italy, from 6 to 22 February 2026.

The Georgian team consisted of eight athletes (four per gender) competing in two sports: alpine skiing and figure skating.[[1]](#cite_note-1) Figure skaters [Luka Berulava](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Berulava "Luka Berulava") and [Diana Davis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diana_Davis "Diana Davis") were the country's flagbearer during the [opening ceremony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Winter_Olympics_opening_ceremony "2026 Winter Olympics opening ceremony").[[2]](#cite_note-2)[[3]](#cite_note-3) Meanwhile, [Luka Berulava](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Berulava "Luka Berulava") and [Nino Tsiklauri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nino_Tsiklauri "Nino Tsiklauri") were the country's flagbearer during the [closing ceremony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Winter_Olympics_closing_ceremony "2026 Winter Olympics closing ceremony").[[4]](#cite_note-4)[[5]](#cite_note-5)

On 16 February, [Luka Berulava](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Berulava "Luka Berulava") and [Anastasiia Metelkina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anastasiia_Metelkina "Anastasiia Metelkina") won the silver medal in the [figure skating pairs event](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Figure_skating_at_the_2026_Winter_Olympics_–_Pair_skating "Figure skating at the 2026 Winter Olympics – Pair skating"), marking the country's first ever [Winter Olympic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winter_Olympic "Winter Olympic") medal.[[6]](#cite_note-6)
